html:
The Jaffna Kingdom was a Tamil kingdom in the north of Sri Lanka from about 1215 to 1619, ruled for most of that time by the Aryacakravarti kings from Nallur near Jaffna.

It rose after the invader Kalinga Magha broke the Polonnaruwa kingdom and power on the island split. It held the pearl fisheries of the Gulf of Mannar and for a time took tribute from Sinhalese kings to the south. The Portuguese annexed it in 1619 and pulled down the great temple at Nallur, rebuilt in the 18th century.

The kingdom gave the north its Tamil and Hindu character. The memory of a Tamil state on the island later fed the call for Tamil Eelam in the civil war.
sum: The Jaffna Kingdom was a Tamil kingdom in the north of Sri Lanka from about 1215 to 1619, ruled for most of that time by the Aryacakravarti kings from Nallur near Jaffna.
